summary: Repaired both bundle symlinks as relative links. They work in place, after copying to another directory, and after restarting node1. Ubuntu 24.04 and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were preserved.
actions_performed: Changed bundle/current to point to releases/two.
Changed bundle/latest-report to point to releases/two/report.txt.
Verified both entries remain symlinks, match links.tsv, and resolve successfully.
Verified regular-file SHA-256 checksums remained unchanged.
Copied the bundle to a temporary directory and verified both links and report contents there.
Safely restarted node1, confirmed its boot ID changed, and repeated health, persistence, checksum, and relocation tests.

evidence.requirement: Repair absolute symlinks while preserving their intended targets and link type
evidence.summary: Initial inspection recorded the manifest and absolute links; subsequent commands show current -> releases/two and latest-report -> releases/two/report.txt as resolving relative links.

evidence.requirement: Bundle must work when copied to another directory
evidence.summary: Independent pre- and post-restart copy tests resolved both links and read 'Report release two' through each copied link.
Pre-change and post-change SHA-256 hashes match; post-restart assertions also report regular_file_hashes=UNCHANGED.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Before and after work, node1 reports Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic.

Healthy baseline boot ID bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49 was captured, the safe restart was acknowledged, availability returned with changed boot ID 7c3c316b-ad58-4102-af5e-cca7fa0d3623, and system/data/link health fully recovered.
